correct_answer: The B&P pool decreases by $192,000 (base costs only); the FY25 OH pool decreases by $88,040 (OH backed out per Linda's DM); the missing approval is the CAS-required written notification to the CFAO of a change in cost accounting practice.
rationale: Linda's Teams DM (the critical informal signal) confirms that both the $192K base cost AND the $88,040 OH should be backed out of their respective pools. The B&P pool drops by $192K (base costs) and the OH pool drops by $88,040 (overhead that was allocated to those B&P costs). The overhead gets reapplied at the CEDAR-OPS rate (58%) on the new project. The missing approval is the CAS notification: moving costs from an indirect pool (B&P) to direct charging represents a change in cost accounting practice under CAS 9904.402. The contractor must notify the CFAO in writing. This isn't a DCAA pre-approval (DCAA audits but doesn't approve; Answer D misattributes authority). The contract language provides the FAR 31.205-32 basis for allowability, but CAS compliance is a separate obligation — the CO's consent (Answer B) is already embedded in the contract clause. Answer B incorrectly includes the full $280K as the B&P reduction (the $88K is OH pool, not B&P pool) and misses the CAS notification requirement entirely.
